# ui::CubicBezier

Header: `winui/render/CubicBezier.hpp`.

A cubic Bézier easing curve. The start and end anchors are fixed at (0,0) and (1,1), with the elapsed-time fraction in and the progress fraction out, both 0..1, so only the two interior control points are given. The default, [`easing::Linear`](namespace-ui-easing.md#linear), is a straight ramp, which is what [BrushTransition](../tree/brush-transition.md) always uses. [ScalarTransition](../tree/scalar-transition.md) and [Vector3Transition](../tree/vector3-transition.md) use a (0.8,0)-(0.2,1) curve. [`easing::ControlFastOutSlowIn`](namespace-ui-easing.md#controlfastoutslowin) is the curve the rest of the themed motion uses. Its control points (0,0)-(0,1) make it a pure decelerate, fast at the start and slow at the end.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::CubicBezier ease_out{0.1f, 0.9f, 0.2f, 1.0f};
const float halfway = ui::easing::evaluate(ease_out, 0.5); // progress at half the time
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x1` | `float` | `0.0f` | The two interior control points, (x1,y1) and (x2,y2), each coordinate 0..1 (x is time, y is progress). The default is the linear ramp. |
| `y1` | `float` | `0.0f` |  |
| `x2` | `float` | `1.0f` |  |
| `y2` | `float` | `1.0f` |  |
